title: Scaling your startup, Team: hiring generalists, outsourcing, firing and equity
summary: Jason Calacanis and the Launch team walk through building a startup team: who to hire first, in-house versus outsourced work, hiring outreach, org structure, firing, and compensation. Jason's main points: keep engineering in-house, hire missionaries, explain the why behind goals, fire kindly but firmly, and let candidates choose cash or equity.

principles.text: Early hires wear many hats; specialization emerges as the company grows into departments.
principles.quote: it goes from having one person do five jobs to five people do five jobs to five people doing one job and that's called a department

principles.text: Keep developers in-house; dev shops don't build company knowledge and slow your pace.
principles.quote: when you hire those dev shops you don't accrue the knowledge into the company and then you can't move as fast because you're waiting on some dev shop that has four different customers

principles.text: Run the team at about 80% capacity to avoid burnout and leave room for special projects.
principles.quote: one way to make your organization grow is to say I'm going to keep everybody at 80 percent which is what I like to do here

principles.text: Write personal job posts and hire missionaries, not mercenaries.
principles.quote: you really want missionaries not mercenaries

principles.text: Explain the reason behind each goal; startup employees want to know why.
principles.quote: I think that's really the heart the hardest thing about being a manager today is that you're dealing with and a start-up people who want to know why

principles.text: Offer candidates a choice between more cash or more equity.
principles.quote: I'll offer um $80,000 plus one percent of the company or ninety thousand dollars and fifty basis points or a hundred thousand dollars and twenty basis points and let them pick which one they want
